This review provides an overview of recent advances in the enantioselective synthesis of α-stereogenic ketones, highlighting emerging strategies beyond classical chemistry, such as radical reactions, nucleophilic reactions, acyl–nickel-enabled cross-coupling, and enzyme-catalyzed dehalogenation.
n5b1cbf4def2e: Pure-iodide wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites (∼1.68 eV) featuring eliminated photoinduced halide segregation are compelling top-cell absorbers for perovskite-silicon tandem solar cells. More importantly, the associated perovskite-silicon solar cells deliver a stabilized PCE of 30.74% along with improved thermal stability, highlighting the great potential of pure-iodide WBG perovskites for efficient and durable tandem photovoltaics.
nea3b036467e1: Ceria-based thermochemical cycles offer a promising route to solar hydrogen, but require reduction above 1400 °C and large temperature swings. ncc880a219f5a: Ionomer engineering offers a powerful yet underexplored strategy for electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR), since the polymer tailors the microenvironment at the catalyst surface. The AEI-modified commercial Cu nanoparticle electrode reaches an NH3 yield rate of 13.8 mg h–1cm–2 and 98.0% Faradaic efficiency, positioning the fixed-charge sign and hydration as accessible design descriptors potentially transferable to other electrocatalytic reactions.

nbacb4ba04329: Gold nanoclusters have long been limited in optoelectronic applications by sub-picosecond hot-carrier cooling. n89e8ac68b1d8: Strain-release cycloadditions have emerged as powerful reactions for converting distorted ring systems into complex and otherwise hardly attainable organic molecular architectures. This Review encompasses the fundamentals of strain, its role in governing cycloaddition pathways, and offers a systematic examination of strained carbocycles and heterocycles, from bicyclo[1.1.1]butanes and 1-azabicyclo[1.1.1]butanes, housanes and aza-housanes, 2H-azirines and aziridines, azetidines, cyclopropanes, cyclobutanes, oxiranes, oxetanes, and strained alkynes and alkenes. Across these motifs, the general principles that dictate reactivity, the breadth of known cycloadditions and activation strategies, from Brønsted and Lewis acid catalysis to transition-metal activation, photocatalysis, and double strain-release mechanisms, are highlighted. Key opportunities, current limitations, and future directions are outlined.
nbb3af51a923a: This review focuses on recent advances of asymmetric hydrogenation in the strategic total synthesis of natural products and drug molecules, and outlines future perspectives for this field.
ne7b758fb2af0: This Tutorial Review establishes a unified framework connecting the fundamentals of solar vapor generation with materials and structural design, providing guiding principles for efficient, scalable, and sustainable water production.
n61f901993ff1: Dual-atom alloys (DAAs) embedded in metallic surfaces constitute an emerging catalytic platform fundamentally distinct from the widely studied carbon-supported dual-atom sites, as they enable intrinsic metal–metal cooperation within an active metallic environment. However, a systematic understanding of their structure–stability relationships remains elusive, mainly due to the prohibitive cost of exploring the vast space of compositions, crystal surfaces, and atomic configurations. Here, using Cu-based DAAs as a prototypical platform, we construct a library of 6804 candidate structures spanning nine crystal planes and two representative dual-atom configurations. Density functional theory (DFT)-calculated formation energies for 930 representative structures (13.7% of the library) are employed to train a physics-informed residual multilayer perceptron model combined with 5-fold ensemble learning. The model achieves high predictive accuracy with cross-validation R2 > 0.906 and demonstrates robust transferability across different crystal planes and structural motifs, outperforming conventional machine-learning baselines. Interpretable SHAP analysis indicates that electronic structure descriptors predominantly govern stability, with geometric compatibility contributing as a secondary factor. Systematic stability trends are identified, including a thermodynamic preference for diagonal configurations on the (100), (311), and (411) surfaces, linear-close configurations on the (110), (111), and (211) surfaces, and enhanced stability for noble-metal dopants, such as Au, Pt, and Pd. Electronic structure analysis further establishes a clear correlation between formation energy and the dopant d-band center, with greater stability achieved when the d-band center is located farther from the Fermi level. With the training on a limited number of DFT-calculated samples, this physics-aware and transferable machine-learning framework enables rapid and data-efficient prediction of dual-atom alloy stability. The approach is readily extensible to diverse crystal surfaces and alloy systems, providing a generalizable theoretical foundation for the thermodynamic screening and rational design of DAAs with high synthetic feasibility in energy catalysis.
n1e296c89bac2: Crystal facet engineering tailors a self-adaptive microenvironment for acidic OERs. The α-MnO 2 {100} facet forms a hydroxyl-rich interface that stabilizes Ir single atoms and lowers water-oxidation barriers, improving activity and stability.

n03dd40dd7715: The unstable ITO-SAM interface limits organic solar cell efficiency and stability. nb55bfa734a4d: Temperature can influence competing catalytic pathways differently, but its role in balancing electrocatalytic activity and stability remains underexplored. nd1125c45a8c2: Buried-interface engineering is critical for inverted perovskite solar cells, yet integrating anchoring, charge transport, electrostatic regulation, and defect passivation within single molecular systems often creates intrinsic trade-offs. n053a91296ef7: Pure-water membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) represent a promising strategy to eliminate (bi)carbonate salt precipitation for electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2R). n6bade4f80897: Integrating alternative oxidation reactions (AORs) into photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems is promising for unassisted hydrogen production and value-added chemical synthesis, yet organic semiconductor (OS) photoanodes suffer from poor charge extraction and short carrier lifetimes. n7346fcd5e078: Interface engineering has emerged as a critical strategy for advancing perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs), enabling remarkable improvements in the device efficiency, stability, and spectral purity. We then survey advanced characterization techniques, including photoelectron spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, and time-resolved optical methods, that elucidate interfacial energy-level alignment, defect states, charge dynamics, and degradation pathways. On the basis of these insights, we systematically discuss versatile engineering strategies, such as self-assembled monolayers, dipole interlayers, dimensional regulation, and passivation schemes, to mitigate non-radiative recombination, balance charge fluxes, and enhance operational stability. Finally, we highlight emerging applications spanning high-resolution displays, flexible lighting, and lasing while outlining key challenges and future directions toward commercial realization. This Review aims to offer a holistic framework linking interfacial design to device performance, guiding next-generation PeLED development.
n65cca399b7fe: The interfacial electron-transfer process acts as a pivotal kinetic determinant of electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency, governing the generation of excited-state emitters and thus dictating the intensity and stability of ECL signals. However, most of these luminophores exhibit low ECL efficiency in aqueous media, and the intrinsic reaction and activation mechanisms remain ambiguous because of their complex structures and compositions. Notably, tuning electron-transfer pathways at the molecular/atomic level can not only enable efficient signal amplification but also facilitate the tracking of reaction pathways, thereby providing deeper insights into the fundamental mechanisms underlying ECL processes. This Review comprehensively summarizes advances during the past five years in tuning interfacial electron transfer to enhance ECL. Furthermore, we highlight progress in electron-transfer-mediated signal amplification strategies for highly sensitive ECL biosensing and bioimaging applications. Finally, we propose and discuss the challenges and perspectives associated with improving the ECL efficiency through the modulation of electron transfer processes. Precise regulation of interfacial electron transfer holds substantial promise for advancing ECL theories, clarifying reaction mechanisms, and expanding the scope of ECL-based bioanalytical applications.

n874a803e9337: Rechargeable magnesium (Mg) metal batteries are promising high-energy-density alternatives to lithium-ion systems, yet sluggish cathode kinetics hinder their development. n7b18684a7f4e: Leveraging oxygen redox in lithium-rich layered oxides paves the way for increasing the energy density of lithium-ion batteries, whose practical implementation is plagued by poor stability. Here, we show that Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is derived by the precursor structure according to the degree of transition-metal separation. Furthermore, it is corroborated that cathodes with more dispersed Li2MnO3-like ordering derived from less-ordered precursors exhibit improved electrochemical stability with a mitigated voltage decay. Our findings highlight the significance of precursor design and engineering for structural regulation of high-performance lithium-rich layered oxide cathodes.
n8d648f4076f8: The rational combination of multiple electrolyte additives is a promising strategy for constructing stable interphases in lithium-ion batteries. However, unintended additive interactions can alter the preferential reduction/oxidation pathways at electrode surfaces, compromising cell performance. Specifically, an electron-deficient boron-embedded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from LiBOB promotes the reduction of the electron-rich nitrile moieties of SN, disrupting fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)-driven SEI construction. Based on this mechanism, SN was replaced with triisopropanolamine borate (TPAB), which mitigates transition metal dissolution through its amine moiety while forming a robust borate-based cathode electrolyte interphase. Moreover, TPAB combined with LiBOB avoided detrimental side reductions at the anode–electrolyte interface. The FEC-LiBOB-TPAB combination creates thermally stable interphases on the Gr-Si anode and LiNi0.91Co0.08Al0.01O2 cathode (4.8 mAh cm–2), enabling 68.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 45 °C and 1C.
n03850d8c938a: Polymer film capacitors are fundamental to modern power electronics, yet low permittivity restricts their energy density. Although poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) possesses high intrinsic permittivity, stabilizing its polar structure remains thermodynamically challenging. Here, we report a scalable physical processing strategy to optimize PVDF-based films via a specialized shear-imposed coating methodology. By employing a micro-structured blade, we generate intense local shear flow fields that exert hydrodynamic tension to drive a coil-stretch transition. This process drives an α-to-β phase transition and templates the growth of oriented, polar-phase-rich crystal structures. Furthermore, we develop a stage-wise regulation strategy using binary solvents to orchestrate evaporation dynamics, effectively trapping these metastable shear-induced conformations before relaxation. Effective across the PVDF copolymer family, this method enables P(VDF-HFP) films to achieve a high energy density of 20.05 J/cm3, a 44% improvement over conventional casting. This work provides a general, non-chemical pathway for manufacturing high-performance functional polymers through multi-physical field synergistic regulation.

n80fcdd851a13: An atomically precise, ligand-capped Cu49 nanocluster is demonstrated to efficiently catalyze the semihydrogenation of alkynes at room temperature. nb91102874037: While polyester waste represents a valuable carbon resource for chemical production, its upcycling typically involves multiple steps for polymer depolymerization, intermediate separation, and subsequent conversion. n7c477b3c2b75: Facing global freshwater scarcity and energy shortages, this work designs a flower-inspired 3D solar evaporator made from modified ramie yarns that simultaneously generates clean water and electricity. n8662555b8320: Although organosilicon compounds containing different carbon substituents are ubiquitous in synthetic chemistry, their preparation is challenging. Laboratory synthesis commonly relies on the sequential substitution of tetrachlorosilane or tetraalkoxysilanes, producing complex mixtures that require demanding purification. This arises from limited control over nucleophilic substitution in functionalized silanes containing three or four (identical) leaving groups. Here we introduce an experimentally straightforward and reliable procedure for the preparation of both hetero- and homoleptic silanes using an overlooked monobromination of primary and secondary hydrosilanes. An equimolar amount of elemental bromine converts a Si–H bond into an Si–Br bond without ‘overbromination’. This step also shows exceptional functional-group tolerance to existing substituents at the silicon atom. Unsaturated moieties as well as heteroatom and heteroaryl groups are compatible. When performed in an iterative fashion, multihydrosilanes can be selectively converted into secondary, tertiary and quaternary silanes with two, three or four different carbon substituents in high yields. These functionalized silicon building blocks are relevant to synthetic chemistry as well as applied chemistry materials.
n2f6e6b14dbd3: The stepwise installation of carbon substituents at silicon starting from tetrachlorosilane or tetraalkoxysilanes is burdened by chemoselectivity issues, typically affording product mixtures. n617dd9db8a0f: Advances in dynamic covalent chemistry have dramatically broadened its use in polymer research. This review summarizes recent advances in dynamic polymer chemistry based on cyclic disulfide bonds that have enabled new design principles for the development and innovation in advanced polymers. We highlight living/controlled polymerization strategies for cyclic disulfide monomers, covering the principal polymerization strategies and mechanisms, and discuss the future challenges and prospective directions of the field in the context of emerging societal and technological demands.

ned9501745b95: Transition metal fluorides (TMFs) are promising conversion-type cathode materials for high-energy lithium–metal batteries owing to their exceptionally high theoretical energy density, making them attractive for demanding applications such as electric aviation. However, their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish conversion kinetics, pronounced voltage hysteresis, and poor electrochemical reversibility. Understanding the structural and chemical evolution of TMFs and the electrode–electrolyte interphase formed during cycling is essential for improving their performance. Monodisperse nanocrystalline TMFs are ideal model systems for high-resolution transmission electron microscopy because their uniform size, morphology, and electron transparency enable representative nanoscale characterization. Here, we investigate a reproducible colloidal synthesis of monodisperse, single-crystalline CoF2 nanorods and elucidate the mechanisms governing their formation to achieve precise control over particle size and aspect ratio. By independently varying reaction time, temperature, precursor composition, and ligand chemistry, we identify the key factors controlling precursor decomposition, burst nucleation, phase selection, and anisotropic crystal growth. These insights provide a transferable framework for the controlled synthesis of a broad range of transition metal fluoride nanocrystals.

n37d5bb016408: The bacterial surface represents the primary interface between pathogens and hosts, yet its chemical and architectural complexity challenges conventional classification. This Review examines structural organization, molecular composition, and biogenesis of bacterial surface components across the Gracilicutes and Terrabacteria clades, linking mechanistic detail to pathogenic function. We describe lipid diversity, integral membrane protein biogenesis, and lipoprotein processing at the inner membrane and how these components support surface remodeling, secretion, and virulence. We then examine the peptidoglycan layer and its role in immune recognition and surface protein display, teichoic acids and their contributions to antimicrobial resistance and immune evasion, and S layers, whose crystalline arrays mediate adhesion and immune modulation. The outer membrane section covers lipopolysaccharide biosynthesis, outer membrane protein biogenesis and folding, lipoprotein trafficking, and contributions to pathogenicity, while the mycobacterial section addresses the mycolyl-arabinogalactan-peptidoglycan complex and virulence factors. We discuss bacterial capsule diversity, biosynthesis, and use as vaccine antigens, along with adhesive surface structures such as fimbriae, pili, and curli fibers and their roles in colonization and biofilm formation, before covering secretion systems types I through XI and their contributions to virulence. This Review provides a framework for understanding how bacterial surface diversity shapes infection and identifies chemical vulnerabilities for therapeutics.
n3f072c4ef5be: Single-atom catalysts (SACs) offer exceptional structural resolution for investigating how local environments govern catalytic behavior and, ultimately, for controlling these effects through catalyst design. Yet, atomic dispersion does not imply a single or fully defined catalytic environment. The behavior of atomically dispersed active centers is shaped by a hierarchical local environment comprising persistent and transient contributions, while also being influenced by an extended reaction environment that intersects with the local environment in controlling reactivity and can become integrated into it. Establishing these boundaries and understanding how these contributions evolve and interact are central challenges in the interpretation and design of SACs. Here, we critically examine how local environments are generated and controlled, experimentally and theoretically resolved across spatial and temporal scales, transformed from synthesis through operation and deactivation, and linked to catalytic performance through structural, energetic, and electronic descriptors. By integrating aspects that are often considered separately and highlighting those that remain insufficiently addressed, we provide a roadmap toward the predictive, environment-driven design of SACs and a deeper understanding of catalytic phenomena.
n98cc28f955b7: Regenerated cellulose (RC), derived from natural cellulose through dissolution and regeneration processes, has emerged as a sustainable, versatile, and cost-effective material for advanced electronic devices. With unique hierarchical structures, abundant hydroxy groups, and excellent mechanical and thermal properties, RC allows extensive customization of its characteristics, offering biocompatibility, flexibility, processability, and environmental friendliness. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in RC-based electronics, focusing on its multiscale molecular configuration, dissolution and regeneration mechanisms, and functionalization and engineering strategies. It first provides a detailed molecular-level analysis of RC structures and formation mechanisms. The principles and strategies of cellulose dissolution and regeneration are then discussed, with emphasis on solvent systems and structure-regulating mechanisms essential for processing control. Functionalization strategies are categorized into direct modification and hybridization with functional materials. Notably, the hybridization approach involves the development of conductive, semiconductive, and insulating RC composites, evaluated from the perspectives of material selection, interfacial design, and processing techniques. Subsequently, engineering approaches to enhance mechanical strength, electrical conductivity, and optical transparency are explored. Applications of RC in sensors, actuators, circuits, energy harvesting and storage devices, and electromagnetic shielding devices are highlighted, demonstrating its potential to drive sustainable innovation in electronics. Finally, future directions are proposed to address remaining challenges, paving the way for RC to contribute to eco-friendly, high-performance electronic devices.

n8f2204474093: Hydrogen is a promising energy carrier due to its clean and versatile nature, offering opportunities for decarbonizing diverse sectors. Hydrogen utilization in many applications relies on identifying and understanding materials with exceptional hydrogen storage and transport properties. In this study, we conducted a comprehensive investigation of the thermodynamic and kinetic properties of hydrogenation reactions in ternary ABO3 perovskites using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML) screening. We performed DFT simulations for a diverse range of perovskites featuring a variety of A-site cations (Ca, Sr, Ba) and B-site cations (Co, Fe, Mn, Ce, Ti, Zr) across various phases (cubic, tetragonal, orthorhombic, and hexagonal). By computing all data at the same theoretical level, we establish a consistent framework to compare how crystal phase, lattice-site chemistry, and host electronic structure govern hydrogen incorporation and diffusion. Therefore, we identify hexagonal SrMnO3, cubic SrFeO3, and hexagonal BaFeO3 as particularly promising candidates, combining favorable hydrogenation thermodynamics (ΔG < 1 eV) with low rotation and hopping barriers (<0.2 eV), while orthorhombic phases, although thermodynamically preferred, suffer from proton trapping, highlighting the importance of phase engineering toward cubic/hexagonal frameworks. Ab initio molecular dynamics further support this phase-dependent kinetic picture by showing relatively facile H diffusion in cubic SrFeO3 but much slower proton motion in orthorhombic BaCeO3 under the same conditions. By incorporating spatial and electronic descriptors with the DFT data into our ML models, we further develop a mechanistically motivated ML model based on structural and electronic descriptors to screen hydrogenation thermodynamics across 111 ternary ABO3 compositions. This model led to the identification of two additional promising candidates, hexagonal BaPdO3 and cubic BaSnO3, which were subsequently validated by DFT calculations. These findings provide a foundation for the rational design of ABO3 perovskites and demonstrate the potential of ML-driven frameworks with chemical insights to accelerate materials discovery in energetic and catalytic applications.

n91d94e745e84: Are ether electrolytes inherently hazardous? ne37abb50eb58: Next-generation two-dimensional electronics require robust insulating layers that effectively control current without compromising device performance. n0d952b2b1d7b: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are a class of crystalline, porous networks constructed by polymerization of organic building blocks. Distinct from conventional catalysis, these catalysts interact with monomers, intermediates and transition states, thereby reducing energy barriers at each step and promoting reversibility. This approach enables control through catalyst-to-monomer ratios and allows the rapid synthesis, within hours, of imide-, imine-, hydrazone- and sp2-carbon-linked COFs with high crystallinity and porosity. The method further supports catalyst reuse and 1,000-fold scale-up, producing COFs with benchmark proton conductivity, establishing hydrogen-bonding catalysis as a versatile route for scalable COF synthesis and applications. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are typically synthesized under harsh acid- or base-catalysed conditions. Here a hydrogen-bonding catalysis strategy based on reusable benzimidazole enables the rapid and scalable production of COFs with high crystallinity and porosity, offering a general route to imide, imine, hydrazone and sp2-carbon-linked COF synthesis.

na4e19c33972d: Understanding the dynamic interplay between all components in complex electrocatalytic systems is crucial to advancing their performance. n3f9ff6cc68a9: Two-dimensional infrared (2DIR) spectroscopy has emerged as a powerful tool for probing the structure and picosecond dynamics of complex, condensed-phase systems at the molecular level. In electrolytes and ionic liquids, where physicochemical properties arise from the interplay between solvation and ionic interactions, 2DIR spectroscopy provides unique insights into intermolecular interactions and dynamical processes that are often inaccessible to conventional spectroscopies. This review highlights seminal and recent advances in understanding the behavior of these systems using 2DIR spectroscopy, with particular emphasis on spectral diffusion, vibrational relaxation, and chemical exchange dynamics. The review also describes how complementary information from the vibrational modes of solvents, salts, and external probes enables detailed characterization of ion–ion interactions, hydrogen-bonding networks, and solvation environments, providing a molecular framework of the structure and time evolution of these charged systems. Moreover, particular attention is given to the dynamics of distinct molecular moieties and to the role of specific anions, cations, and solvent environments in governing behavior on femtosecond to picosecond time scales. Finally, the review describes current challenges, including the limited availability of intrinsic vibrational reporters and experimental constraints, and key open questions in electrochemical and energy-relevant systems that remain despite an extensive number of studies in the area.

nc5a177fd0583: Terrestrial electrochemical design implicitly relies on Earth-bound physics, such as gravity and natural convection. nacf5a46e6957: Mechanically generated radicals are often considered detrimental in materials. nd7bb92b5f0b0: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. Thus, the triplet-state lifetime is a key parameter in solid-state upconversion.
n7217e9742006: Extensively fluorinated aramid polymers fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticle tubes with continuous internal lumens. Stabilized by F–H–F interactions, these abiotic channels enable ultrafast and highly selective water transport across membranes, surpassing natural aquaporins while maintaining excellent salt rejection.
n36c28ff1dc93: Marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) techniques have the potential to remove legacy emitted carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it durably in ocean reservoirs. While the ocean’s vast surface area and buffering capacity offer benefits for scaling removal, monitoring remains challenging. This comprehensive review of marine carbonate system observing and monitoring technologies finds that mCDR processes span multiple scales, often at the edges of existing platform and sensing capability. While some mCDR observing and monitoring is possible today, challenges will arise as experiments and operations expand. Leaps forward in assessing the novel scales of mCDR processes will emerge from low-energy, low-cost, highly durable sensors; innovative deployment platforms; cooperative sensing networks; dedicated model validation programs; and decision support tools. This review is intended to serve as a guide to the history, ongoing innovation, and transformative vision of future marine carbonate system observing and monitoring informed by mCDR.
n53094d298fe3: Aqueous Zn-I2 batteries are promising for energy storage, yet suffer from sluggish iodine conversion kinetics and polyiodide shuttling effect, severely limiting the rate capability and cycling durability. Conventional M-N4 single-atom...
n2bd3b6453a01: Organic materials inherently exhibit significant electron-phonon coupling due to the strong dependence of electronic structures on molecular nuclear configurations, often resulting in substantial non-radiative voltage losses (ΔVnr) of organic photovoltaics...
n2c58b2d06982: Light-induced phase segregation limits the efficiency and stability of wide-band-gap mixed-halide perovskites. This work demonstrates that multi-site molecular regulation can cooperatively manage Frenkel defect-pair dynamics, thereby suppressing phase segregation. This stabilization is achieved by thermodynamically suppressing Frenkel defect-pair formation and dissociation while kinetically restricting subsequent halide redistribution.
ne2b86c450632: Nanopore protein sequencing has advanced from a theoretical ambition to a practical technology, overcoming major challenges in protein unfolding, transport and signal detection to achieve single-amino-acid and post-translational modification sensitivity. With both full-length and peptide-based approaches progressing towards commercialization, the field is now focused on scaling throughput and refining analysis tools to unlock a new generation of single-molecule proteomics.
nc78d4c42fe9f: Two decades on from the first atomic-scale devices, atom-based silicon quantum computers have progressed from proof of concept to scalable quantum processors that are rapidly gaining commercial traction. What remains is largely a matter of industrial-scale engineering and 3D integration.
nd96a615d3ec9: As the journal turns 20, we reflect on the journey nanoscale science has undertaken over the past two decades and how nanoscience-enabled technologies have had a real-world impact.
n3b7306b098f3: Quantum dots — semiconductor nanocrystals whose optical and electronic properties can be tuned by controlling their size, composition and surface chemistry — have found commercial success for display technologies. Their transition from nanophotonics research into an applied modern nanotechnology exemplifies the bottlenecks that many emerging technologies must overcome on the path to commercialization.
nb2f1eec7e23b: Curiosity-driven studies of lipid organization and lipid asymmetry in biological membranes led to scalable methods for making liposomes, efficient loading of drugs and ionizable cationic lipids. In turn, these advances led to lipid nanoparticles enabling the RNA medicine Onpattro and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, and they are now facilitating gene therapies that can potentially treat most human diseases.
n2dc08f16a75e: Single-atom catalysis has reshaped heterogeneous catalysis by shifting its central focus from surface and interface to isolated atom-centred active sites. This transition establishes a new paradigm for understanding reactivity, integrating experiments and theory, and advancing heterogeneous catalysis from empirical observations toward a more predictive and precise science.
nf1ff5a986198: Spin-transfer torque magnetoresistive random access memory has emerged as a leading non-volatile memory technology replacing embedded Flash in diverse fields including aerospace, automotive and healthcare applications.
nc6aa8f3cb4a1: After years of hype and research, there is still no graphene battery electrode in mass production, but researchers say the material shows promise for energy storage.
n2e47fb53617f: Tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides display interesting therapeutic properties; however, methods for their synthesis are limited. Now a Rh-catalysed process enables their synthesis through the development of a dual-function directing group that promotes C–H activation and C–N bond formation. The method provides access to a range of macrocycles, including pharmacophores of micitide 982 and tryglysin.
n30d6e5e89e89: Chiral allylic amines are key building blocks in the synthesis of bioactive molecules. Now a regio- and enantioselective method for their synthesis is reported. The Ni-catalysed process proceeds through homologation of enamines by cross-coupling with alkynes, forming a range of chiral allylic amines in good yield and with excellent enantioselectivity.
nf8412247aa79: Single-atom alloys (SAAs) are an emerging class of heterogeneous catalysts that maximize atom efficiency by embedding isolated reactive metal atoms within a host metal surface, creating well-defined active sites. Atomic isolation imparts unique catalytic properties, including high selectivity, resistance to poisoning, coking, and sintering, and in some cases the ability to circumvent conventional scaling relationships that limit traditional catalysts. This article focuses on progress in the SAA field since our 2020 review (Chem. Rev.2020, 120, 12044−12088.), while incorporating earlier foundational studies where relevant. We first examine the fundamental principles governing SAA formation, stability, electronic structure, reactivity, and selectivity, drawing on insights from experimental single-crystal model systems and theoretical studies. We then review the application of SAAs in a wide range of industrially important reactions, including hydrogenation, dehydrogenation, selective oxidation, water–gas shift, Fischer–Tropsch synthesis, and dry reforming, among others. Beyond thermal catalysis, SAAs demonstrate great promise in electrocatalysis and plasmon-driven chemistry. Their structurally simple active sites have also enabled the rational design of novel catalysts and promoters that challenge conventional catalytic intuition. Looking ahead, recent advances in computing, including machine-learning potentials, offer the opportunity to explore vast compositional spaces and discover new alloy chemistries for challenging reactions using the SAA concept.
neaeb3c1505d4: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) have emerged as promising electrochemical energy storage technologies for long-duration stationary applications. Although aqueous RFBs represent the most commercially mature class, they are inherently limited by a narrow electrochemical stability window and high temperature sensitivity. Nonaqueous RFBs (NRFBs) expand the accessible voltage and temperature ranges, offering a promising route toward high-energy-density storage for long-duration and extreme-environment applications. However, their practical deployment remains impeded by several challenges, including high costs, insufficient power density, limited cycling stability, and safety concerns. This review offers a systematic synthesis of recent advances in key NRFB components, encompassing solvents, supporting electrolytes, membranes, electrodes, and redox-active molecules. We also highlight emerging methodologies expected to accelerate development, including machine-learning-enabled screening, advanced characterization, and life cycle assessment. Finally, this review compares aqueous and nonaqueous systems from commercialization and sustainability perspectives. Collectively, this review aims to advance design principles and optimization strategies for NRFBs, providing guidance for next-generation low-cost, high-energy-density flow battery technologies.
nd38b8af0450d: Applicability and uncertainties of the BET analysis for porous materials, and its emerging alternatives.
n9bf97f69680b: Aviation's climate impact goes beyond CO2, yet current policies such as the EU's ReFuelEU regulation push almost exclusively toward sustainable fuels, overlooking an alternative: permanently capturing CO2 from the air via DACCS while continuing to burn fossil jet fuel. Comparing long-term costs of both approaches, we find DACCS is 49%–69% cheaper than synthetic fuels and needs far less renewable electricity, suggesting that current policy may be locking aviation into a costlier decarbonization path than necessary.
n24a7fb176953: Methane pyrolysis can produce hydrogen while sequestering solid carbon, but efficient high-grade heat delivery and coking management remain challenging. This study shows that high-frequency magnetic induction directly and volumetrically heats molten salt bubbling beds with stable power delivery, providing a scalable route for methane pyrolysis while managing solid carbon formation. These principles have applicability more broadly to molten salt chemical conversion and thermal energy storage systems.
n71f3585b7a45: Efforts to improve carbon dioxide electroreduction have often focused on the catalyst. Now, by focusing on the gas instead, non-thermal plasma activation can unlock products that are not accessible through conventional electrocatalysis.
nf495575612b6: Integrating distinct weaving topologies within a single molecular network creates coupled deformation modes and adaptive adsorption behaviour, pointing to a shift from constructing molecular topologies to exploiting them for functions.
n860fed4f84de: Four-membered heterocycles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, yet valuable thietanes remain underexplored compared with widely studied oxetanes and azetidines. Now a one-step skeletal editing strategy is reported that directly converts oxetanes into thietanes using thiourea.
n8cf20cf25776: Research on enantioselective photocatalysis has so far been focused on molecular photocatalysts or large yet easily adaptable photoenzymes. However, both catalysis classes display deficiencies either due to their limited adaptability or their high molecular weight. Here we show that small peptides can bridge the gap between the currently used photocatalysts by combining structural flexibility and low molecular weight. We constructed a small peptide that displays a pyroglutamic acid at its N terminus for substrate recognition. At the C terminus, a thioxanthone-based amino acid was installed to harvest photons and to act catalytically by energy transfer. Two amino acids were sufficient to link the two components, resulting in a photocatalytically active tetrapeptide that was used both for photochemical deracemization and enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition reactions. Our results demonstrate that small peptides with a molecular weight below 750 Da can act as efficient molecular catalysts for enantioselective photochemical transformations.
neab46ce06322: Heteroleptic silylium ions with different substituents at the silicon atom are generally not accessible using established tools for producing such reactive intermediates because substituent exchange reactions occur in acidic media, leading to homoleptic silylium ions with three identical alkyl and aryl substituents, respectively. Here we report a broadly applicable route to heteroleptic silylium ions using halosilanes as silylium ion precursors, which are less prone to that scrambling process. While this deceptively simple method has failed so far owing to the lack of a suitable halide-abstracting agent, superhalophilic halogen-substituted silylium ions enable smooth halide abstraction from a diverse set of halosilanes at ambient temperature without substituent redistribution. Accordingly, this approach provides access to essentially any heteroleptic acyclic as well as cyclic silylium-ion motif from common halosilanes, including trialkyl-, dialkyl(aryl)-, alkyldiaryl- and triaryl-substituted congeners. Computational calculations reveal the mechanism of heteroleptic silylium-ion formation and the origin of the suppressed substituent-scrambling process.
n815edb2d6801: Phosphorus-mediated reactions that leverage the thermodynamic driving force of phosphorus(III) oxidation are crucial in all areas of the chemical industry. While substantial progress has been made in phosphorus(III/V) redox organocatalysis to develop catalytic alternatives, the rising field of redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis has revealed new modes of phosphorus-based reactivity in chemical transformations without requiring stoichiometric reductants. This review highlights key advances in redox-neutral phosphorus(V) organocatalysis with a focus on fundamental phosphorus(V) reactivity, organized by the catalyst structure and emphasizing its role as a Lewis acid, Brønsted acid/base, nucleophile, superbase, or single-electron transfer agent. We close with remarks connecting established reactivity paradigms that will likely be applied to new generations of phosphorus(V) catalysts capable of solving modern synthetic challenges.
n6449755a8f52: Chiral medium-sized rings, defined herein as 7- to 11-membered cyclic frameworks, are common in bioactive molecules and occupy an important but still underexplored region of drug-like chemical space. Their asymmetric synthesis remains formidably challenging, as conformational flexibility, transannular interactions, and unfavorable entropic and enthalpic factors collectively complicate ring formation and stereocontrol. In recent years, palladium- and iridium-catalyzed asymmetric dipolar cycloadditions and related cascade processes have emerged as effective strategies for building structurally diverse and stereochemically complex medium-sized rings. As such, this review aims to summarize the advances in this emerging field from the perspectives of metal identity, precursor class, and dipole-generation mode, with emphasis on their effects on chemo-, regio-, diastereo-, and enantioselectivity. We also highlight the distinct yet complementary features of Pd and Ir catalysis, as well as current limitations in generality, selectivity, and substrate scope. By combining mechanistic insight with representative applications, this review aims to define the foundations, boundaries, and future opportunities of this rapidly evolving area.
ne8ea3a471102: Nanocrystalline metal halide perovskites are promising light emitters for light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs) because they suppress the intrinsic problem of exciton dissociation through charge confinement within nanocrystalline domains. Although these nanostructures have enabled high-emission efficiencies, such confinement strategies typically result in significantly reduced charge transport. This limitation is attributed to numerous grain boundaries, which induce severe charge carrier scattering and trapping, alongside insulating organic ligands typically introduced for defect passivation and size reduction. Poor charge transport increases the required operating voltage and accelerates device degradation pathways under an electrical bias, leading to limited operational lifetimes. This Review examines material design strategies intended to mitigate the competition between charge confinement and transport across various nanocrystalline perovskites. Specifically, we investigate fundamental crystal nucleation and growth mechanisms and evaluate methods to optimize grain size, aiming to minimize the grain boundary to increase charge transport while maintaining charge confinement. Passivation strategies for defect states are also evaluated, emphasizing the engineering of organic ligands to enhance their electrical conductivity while maximizing the passivation efficacy. In addition, the integration of core/shell architectures is discussed as a promising strategy. By controlling the shell composition, these structures promote efficient charge transport while maintaining high radiative recombination rates. Together, these material design strategies aim to overcome the confinement and transport trade-offs in PeLEDs.
n920522df35e8: Hetero-cycloaddition reactions are powerful, atom-economical strategies for the rapid construction of heterocyclic frameworks from readily available building blocks. Over the past two decades, advances in photochemistry, photocatalysis, and modern excitation strategies have driven remarkable developments in the field. By accessing electronically excited states, light enables cycloaddition pathways inaccessible under classical thermal conditions, providing access to reactive radical, ionic, or excited-state intermediates under mild conditions. Technological advances in light sources and photocatalyst design have improved reaction efficiency, site-, regio-, and stereoselectivity, while considerably expanding the accessible chemical space. Beyond established hetero-[2 + 2], hetero-(3 + 2), and hetero-[4 + 2] processes, new reaction classes, including π–σ hetero-cycloadditions exploiting strained small-ring systems, have emerged as powerful approaches to structurally complex saturated scaffolds of increasing relevance in medicinal chemistry. In this Review, we critically examine the evolution of photochemical hetero-cycloadditions from 2000 to 2026, discussing fundamental concepts and terminology, cycloaddition classes, heterocyclic targets, and activation mechanisms. We highlight the conceptual advances that have shaped modern photochemical hetero-cycloaddition chemistry and conclude by discussing current limitations and future directions for the field.
nf7497579ad2c: This review highlights the role of inter-flake structure in MXene-based sensing and discusses how spacing, orientation, porosity, and inter-flake chemistry can be controlled to influence its sensing performance.
ncb7f2cd79b18: Sulfides catalyse aromatic halogenations but often struggle with less reactive arenes. Now, breaking the symmetry of existing sulfide catalysts allows sulfur orbital interactions that can expand the scope of these reactions.
ne70e3adaa4b9: The structural basis of key intermediates in isopenicillin N synthase catalysis, underlying β-lactam biosynthesis, has remained incomplete. Now time-resolved X-ray free-electron laser studies capture transient states and reveal how protein dynamics and solvent networks govern oxygen activation and ring formation.
ncb27eaff1d98: Tin-based aqueous flow batteries offer high-capacity anodes due to the potential four-electron redox reactions, but irreversible Sn4+/Sn2+ electrochemistry has hindered battery development. Now it has been shown that iodide-mediated intermediate complexes enable reversible Sn4+/Sn2+ conversion and four-electron Sn4+/Sn0 chemistry, yielding a high anolyte energy density and stable long-term operation.
n90d221a7dd18: Krypton-assisted growth of low-loss α-phase tantalum on silicon stays within back-end-of-line semiconductor thermal budgets while delivering state-of-the-art qubit coherence.
n2692be7c489a: This tutorial review introduces the principles of ligand-directed protein modification and compares the chemical strategies that enable selective covalent functionalization of native proteins through ligation, transfer, and catalysis.
n50e1309940bf: Physical mixing as a modular strategy for interfacial reaction-network catalysis, steering complex transformations through intermediate relay, catalytic shunting and thermodynamic cascading.
n33a42d71317f: This review comprehensively summarizes metal-catalyzed sequential double hydrofunctionalization of alkynes (SDHFA), covering diverse reaction types and selectivity patterns, and highlighting representative mechanisms and synthetic applications.
n9a85fd46c41c: Metal halide perovskites are promising photovoltaic materials but are mechanically fragile. Incorporating electrospun nylon nanofibers into the perovskite produces a mechanically reinforced photoactive composite with nearly 6-fold higher fracture energy while preserving photovoltaic performance. The nanofibers also redistribute incident light within the photoabsorber, illustrating how structural reinforcement can be introduced into a functional semiconductor without sacrificing its optoelectronic properties and enable mechanically robust, multifunctional optoelectronic materials.
nf6ed1c982c98: Cell-free gene expression is embedded directly within a microtubule network to generate a genetically programmed active material with complementary biochemical and physical controls.
n6df4855459b7: Quasiparticle condensates are among the most striking solid-state manifestations of quantum physics. Coupling macroscopic real-space wavefunctions to additional degrees of freedom, such as the electron spin, would add valuable control knobs for quantum applications. While creating spin-carrying superconducting condensates has attracted enormous attention, condensates of light-matter hybrids known as exciton–polaritons have lacked an analogous spin-based perspective. Here we demonstrate magnetically tunable exciton–polariton condensation in the van der Waals magnet CrSBr. Under photoexcitation, CrSBr microwires embedded in an optical cavity show the hallmarks of polariton condensation. Owing to the strong coupling between the spin order and excitonic correlation, the energy of the condensate can be tuned by up to 10.5 meV by an external magnetic field of 2 T. Our results establish CrSBr microcavities as a powerful platform for exploring magnetic control of polariton condensates and mark an essential step towards spin-controlled coherent quantum light sources.
nb7180513e44c: Polarization-selective excitation in SnSe reveals anisotropic valley dynamics with distinct channels: one channel with near-unity valley polarization and one channel that rapidly depolarizes through electron–phonon-mediated intervalley scattering.
n6e1e5e4aa141: A beam-shift-based 4D EMCD method is developed that can map 3D spin vectors across individual atomic planes and reveal how competing spin Hamiltonian interactions drive asymmetric spin rotation in canted antiferromagnetic YFeO3.
nc79c85df6aef: Oxetanes are strained four-membered oxygen heterocycles that are valuable motifs for modulating lipophilicity, metabolic stability and three-dimensional structure of pharmaceuticals. Diaryloxetanes with 3,3-substitution are recognized as bioisosteres of diaryl ketones that preserve key electronic features while exhibiting distinct reactivity. However, synthesis of this motif largely relies on Lewis acid-promoted Friedel–Crafts reactions, which are restricted to electron-rich arenes and often suffer from low functional-group tolerance and competing side reactions. Here we report a method for the synthesis of 3,3-substituted diaryloxetanes from readily available 3-oxetanone through a cross-coupling reaction with tetrafluoropyridone as leaving group. The difunctionalization through subsequent addition of two aryl groups, one from an aryl halide, the other from an arylboronic ester, provides access to a variety of benzophenone bioisosteres. The nickel-catalysed cross-coupling at a fully substituted carbon centre is enabled through oxetanyl C–O bond oxidative addition and establishes programmable entry to 3,3-diaryloxetane bioisosteres that are synthetically challenging to access via traditional polar bond disconnection strategies. Mechanistic studies support a Ni(0)-mediated oxidative addition of the oxetanyl tetrafluoropyridine ester.
ne95f526e57ed: In this issue, we focus on the development of self-driving laboratories for the autonomous synthesis of molecules and materials, with a particular focus on industrial considerations and applications.
n203092372d4a: Anthropogenic nitrogen fixation and nitrification exceed natural denitrification capacity, disrupting the nitrogen cycle and causing environmental pollution. Electrocatalytic inorganic-to-organic nitrogen conversion is promising for restoring this balance. However, diverse product formation makes selectivity control a key challenge. This review examines the conversion of hydroxylamine (NH2OH) as the pivotal precursor bridging inorganic nitrogen oxides (NOX−/NOX) and C–N bond formation toward value-added organonitrogen compounds. We survey the theoretical principles governing NH2OH selectivity, discuss catalytic mechanisms for subsequent C–N bond construction, and review catalyst modulation strategies for organonitrogen synthesis. By framing NH2OH as a linchpin linking denitrification and synthesis, this review outlines key challenges and provides a unified framework connecting fundamental understanding to rational catalyst design for sustainable nitrogen conversion.
n042ed3716da9: This review outlines progress in O- and N-centered radical net-1,2-HAT reactions, covering mechanisms and synthetic applications. The core mechanism, radical translocation from a heteroatom to an α-carbon, enables subsequent coupling or cascades.
ne113ebbf360b: This review discusses exciton behaviour, structural design strategies, spectroscopic probes, and charge-transfer pathways in covalent organic framework photocatalysts to advance efficient solar-to-chemical energy conversion.
n25bd47520a52: This review summarizes the use of porphyrinoids with molecular down-converters in intramolecular SF (i-SF) and molecular up-converters in intramolecular triplet–triplet energy transfer and triplet–triplet annihilation upconversion.
n110dc5a3fe1f: The construction of complex sugars from aldehydes is difficult. Now, a rhodium-catalysed triple-carbonylation cascade is developed that enables the direct conversion of diverse aldehydes into structurally defined 4-carbothreofuranoses in one step. This strategy overcomes long-standing challenges in iterative carbonylation and establishes a modular platform for oxygen-rich scaffold assembly.
ncc309793c241: Controlling the regio-, chemo-, and enantioselectivity of vicinal addition across olefins remains a challenging process. Now, a palladium-catalysed system has been developed, starting from propargylic alcohol precursors, that exploits tiered nucleophilicity between inner- and outer-sphere processes for precise control over the reaction outcome.
n2c56d09d05b8: Interactions between polar molecules are expected to become increasingly strong at low collision energies through dipole–dipole forces. Now it has been shown that ammonia molecules instead exhibit suppressed dipolar interactions in the cold regime as the dipole moment effectively switches off, as shown by local maxima in the collision cross-sections.
ne92e6f29154f: The selective assembly of multiple chemicals into complex chiral architectures in a single operation is a long-standing challenge. Now a palladium-catalysed orthogonal strategy has been shown to sort and incorporate two native N–H/O–H nucleophiles with similar reactivity, delivering enantioenriched 1,2-amino alcohols and 1,2-diols with high selectivity.
n449e45ea3d29: Nitroarenes are unstable in microbial cultures, limiting the biomanufacturing of these industrially and pharmaceutically important chemicals. Genome engineering of nitroreductase-deficient E. coli strains has now been shown to improve nitroarene retention during fermentation, expanding access to nitro functional group chemistry in whole-cell biocatalysis, metabolic engineering and synthetic biology.
nc3887ef9e85e: Carbon capture with conventional mixed-matrix membranes is limited by the inability to achieve high packing densities of porous fillers while preserving their intrinsic transport properties. Here the authors develop high-performance membranes based on single-crystal covalent organic framework fillers using a weak-interaction inlaying strategy that enables high filler loadings.
n9a649f4ee0ec: An adsorption–conversion strategy enables the synthesis of ultrathin intermetallics across a broad compositional space, from binaries to high-entropy alloys.
nfce97253ce26: Optical loss is usually treated as a limitation. An electrically tunable carbon-nanotube layer instead uses directional dissipation to reshape nanoscale polariton propagation.
n590917a4092f: Earlier this year, we packed up a small version of our world and headed to Bird Rock Elementary in La Jolla, California, to meet two dozen second graders waiting to do science. We brought with us a plant molecular farming lab, plush virus nanoparticles, and enough curiosity to fill a classroom. We began with wonder.
